column1: # The FFI bench gate record: one line per check, the target it runs on, the
# .tono it compiles, and the outcome scripts/check-ffi-bench.sh must observe.
# A check that ends elsewhere than recorded fails the gate, in both
# directions: a regression on a green row, and a red row that starts passing
# (update this record and README.md together, that is the progress report).
# outcome: pass | frontend-red | check-red | gen-red | build-red | test-red | run-red | refused
# id
bench
bench
bench
01-go-interface-handle
# 02: the handle is held as the concrete type the Rust block spells, and the
# trait method is reached through its own path, which is what brings the
# trait into scope.
02-rust-foreign-name
03-rust-concrete-types
04-go-variadic-options
05-rust-handle-collection
06-nested-call
# 07: the options form's Rust block names the library's own type and spells
# the field as Option<u8>, so the literal wraps the value in Some(..).
07-rust-struct-literal
08-ts-new-construction
09-ts-sync-method
10-ownership-refused
# 11: the callee is the foreign type itself (FormulaCalculator.parse); Go has
# no static method and nothing to refuse: its block writes the package
# function the library exposes there.
11-ts-static-method
11-rust-static-method
11-go-package-function
# 12: the call passes a declared handle's class itself (instantiate(AnswerCalculator));
# Rust and Go have no type as a value, so their rows pass by being refused.
12-ts-class-reference
12-rust-class-reference-refused
12-go-class-reference-refused
# 13: the library's Client shares its name with the generated entry's; the
# spelling is the library's and keeps the package selector either way.
13-go-name-collision
13-rust-name-collision
13-ts-name-collision
# 14: a generated type inside a spelling is referenced by its own name
# (`Memo[.reading]`), never found by matching a word against the module.
14-go-generated-type-reference
14-rust-generated-type-reference
14-ts-generated-type-reference
# 15: an argument that must convert at the boundary (an i64 into a narrower
# numeric parameter): TypeScript converts across the bigint divide
# (Number(..)), Go writes its builtin conversion (int(..)), and Rust has no
# implicit numeric narrowing, so its generation refuses the binding naming
# both types (refused, as intended).
15-ts-argument-coercion
15-go-argument-coercion
15-rust-numeric-refused
# 16: the constructor takes a pointer to its options struct. The argument
# spells the crossing (`options { .. }: #(&Options)`) and the form's block
# keeps the plain type, so the form's own probe and the call site compile
# together (a `&` on the block satisfied the call and broke the probe).
16-go-pointer-argument
# 17: the value comes from a method of the object the call returned
# (Read(ctx, key).Result()): Go writes the chain as one expression; Rust and
# TypeScript refuse it, since @async names one call and a chain has two.
17-go-value-from-returned-object
17-ts-value-from-returned-object-refused
17-rust-value-from-returned-object-refused
# 18: the constructor returns only the handle (Dial(addr) *Client), next to
# one that returns (T, error). Omitting yields: is the convention; a yields:
# with no returns: is the call's whole signature, so `(c: session)` binds one
# value and implies no error.
18-go-infallible-constructor
# 19: a generic with a bound (Bounded<T extends object>) and a composition
# that consumes two handles (boundedFallback(a, b)). The handle's generated
# interface declares the return the .tono declares, so T instantiates; an
# interface answering unknown cannot satisfy the bound.
19-ts-bounded-generic
# 20: the library takes the class of one of the module's own structs and
# constructs the instance itself (instantiateInto(name, clazz, mappings)).
# TypeScript declares an empty class beside the struct's interface for the
# library to construct; Rust and Go have no type as a value, so their rows
# pass by being refused, as capability 12's do. The mappings table is a Map
# on the library's side and a plain object on the generated side, both
# ways: with the class reference alone this row was build-red (tsc: Record
# is not a Map at the argument, and the handle's Map answer does not
# overlap the declared Record); the spelled crossings turned it green.
20-ts-class-reference-generated-struct
20-go-class-reference-generated-struct-refused
20-rust-class-reference-generated-struct-refused
